newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says deregulation package in final stage.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says deregulation package in final stage.

text.p: Indonesian State Secretary Murdiono said on Wednesday the government's economic deregulation package was almost complete and promised no surprises.
"It (the package) is not delayed. The deregulation package has been designed and I think it is at the final stage now," Murdiono told reporters.
"The government views deregulation as a process that will be taken continuously. The government will not take a surprise move," he said. He did not say when the package would be released, however.
Saleh Afiff, the Coordinating Minister for Economics and Finance, was quoted on June 20 as saying there were differences of opinions among ministers involved in drawing up the package.
Murdiono said that was not surprising.
"I think differences are normal. Certainly every minister will see from his point of view and other ministers from their points of view. There is a need for coordination," Murdiono said.

The World Bank, in its latest report on Indonesia, said that Indonesia's deregulation programme was losing momentum and that this could affect the health of the economy. The Indonesian government routinely unveils measures aimed at bolstering economic growth ahead of the meeting of the Consultative Group on Indonesia (CGI), a grouping of donor nations and financial institutions led by the World Bank. The group is to meet next month in Tokyo.
